extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, USPTO respondents, OED staff, and attorneys who practice before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedural rules, and sanctioning criteria used by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) in resolving misconduct by registered patent practitioners (including specified regulatory provisions and the processes for probation, suspension, publication, and enforcement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for USPTO disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes statutory and regulatory authority for OED and the USPTO Director to consider, approve settlements, and enter Final Orders resolving disciplinary matters for registered practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 requires reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely pay fees to the Office for which clients had instructed or relied upon the practitioner to pay constitutes a violation of this rule (here, checks to the USPTO returned for insufficient funds).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) — dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) proscribes engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizing payments to the Office drawn on accounts containing insufficient funds, resulting in dishonored payments, is conduct that may violate this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i) — conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i) proscribes engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dishonored payments and related conduct can be treated as behavior that reflects adversely on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to ensure USPTO payments are covered (avoid dishonored checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must ensure funds are available for payments to the USPTO; submitting checks that are returned for insufficient funds breaches professional obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented examples: eight checks submitted (various amounts) returned for insufficient funds; practitioners should not draw USPTO payments on accounts lacking sufficient funds and must inform clients when payments are dishonored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to client when payments are dishonored
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must inform the client when a check or payment to the USPTO has been dishonored and returned for insufficient funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case Respondent informed clients on August 28, 2015 (or other dates shown) that checks had been dishonored; timely notification is part of fulfilling duties of representation and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repayment and returned payment surcharge requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must repay dishonored USPTO fees and pay returned check surcharges (example surcharge amount shown: $50.00).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several matters show repayment plus $50 returned payment surcharge; the Final Order requires repayment of remaining dishonored fees within probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered in sanctioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors such as no prior disciplinary history, voluntary continuing legal education (CLE), and steps taken to repay fees are mitigating considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED and Respondent’s agreed resolution reflected that Respondent had no prior disciplinary history during 41 years and had voluntarily attended a CLE on running a small legal practice; these influenced the agreed sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available and imposed (reprimand, probation, suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible disciplinary actions include public reprimand, probation, and suspension (here, public reprimand and 6-month probation were ordered, with suspension up to 90 days possible upon probation violation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order: (a) public reprimand; (b) six-month probation; (c) repayment conditions during probation; (d) procedures that can lead to immediate suspension for up to 90 days if OED finds noncompliance during probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation enforcement process — Order to Show Cause and Director referral
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED believes the Respondent failed to comply during probation, OED shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to the Respondent’s last address of record, and grant 15 days to respond; after consideration, OED may forward materials to the USPTO Director to request immediate suspension up to 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural steps spelled out: (1) OED issues Order to Show Cause, (2) send to address per 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a), (3) grant 15 days to respond, (4) if OED remains of that opinion, deliver Order to Show Cause, response, evidence and argument to USPTO Director and request suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to use last address of record for service (37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders (e.g., Order to Show Cause) must be sent to the Respondent at the last address of record furnished pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures proper service and opportunity to respond to disciplinary process; procedural compliance required for enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED’s electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice materially consistent with the provided Notice of Public Reprimand and Probation in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notification will state the practitioner’s name, registration number, nature of violations (citing specific 37 C.F.R. provisions), the sanction, facts (e.g., amount and number of dishonored checks), and mitigating factors; publication location URLs provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of suspension for USPTO access (customer numbers and PKI certificates)
rubrics_metrics.description: If suspended, the USPTO will dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates; Respondent may not use or obtain customer numbers or PKI certificates until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three specific consequences: (A) dissociation, (B) prohibition on use during suspension, (C) prohibition on obtaining until reinstated; intended to prevent practice before the Office during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal/review does not stay suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director suspends the Respondent pursuant to the Order to Show Cause procedures, any review or appeal of the suspension shall not postpone or hold the suspension in abeyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures suspension takes immediate effect even if appealed, absent separate relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in future complaints or disciplinary proceedings against Respondent, including as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that this Final Order may be used (1) when addressing future complaints or similar misconduct, and (2) in future disciplinary proceedings as (i) aggravating factor for discipline and/or (ii) to rebut statements by or on Respondent's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement approval and Final Order contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement Agreement submitted by the OED Director and Respondent is subject to approval by the Under Secretary of Commerce for IP and USPTO Director; the Final Order sets forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions found in the Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes that settlement resolves disciplinary action arising from stipulated facts and that the Final Order memorializes the facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties bear their own costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and any Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation of costs between parties in this settlement — no award of costs between parties.
